text.p: Stocks rose Monday with the technology group moving up on positive news on global shipment of personal computers.
The overall market also benefited from an uptick in bonds.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 28.90 points at 6,767.77.
In the broader market, advancing issues outnumbered declines 12-10 on volume of 234 million the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was up 7.17 points to 1,216.46.
Analysts said the market's bounce from three sessions of weakness last week was impressive but they were surprised that stocks were doing as well as they were.

"The market internals aren't wonderful, but the Big Board is doing okay. A lot of Dow stocks are in the process of breaking out to the upside," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Chareter Ltd.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury was up 3/32, with its yield steady at Friday's close of 7.14 percent.
Financial markets seemed to ignore the report of higher-than-expected new home sales for March, which came in at 813,000 while the February number was revised upward to 834,000 from 811,000.

"I'm surprised at the strength in stocks because bond yields are still high, and we are at the start of a week full of economic data which could hit bonds again," said Jim Solloway, diretcor of research at Argus Research.
"The stock market is priced at a level that makes it vulnerable to any decline in bond prices," he said.
On Tuesday, Wall Street will focus on the first quarter Employment Cost Index and April consumer confidence.

The first look at the performance of the overall economy in the first quarter is due Wednesday. The April purchasing manager's report comes Thursday, and Friday brings the eagerly awaited employment report for April.
Solloway said another interest rate hike when Federal Reserve policy-makers meet on May 20 was "already cooked into prices." But he said that uncertainty about the course of Fed action remained.

"Investors shouldn't worry so much about the next increase," he said. "The question is how many more tightenings will there be before the Fed stops. No one has a good handle on that. I don't think we'll end with just one more increase.
Technology stocks rallied on news that global unit shipments of personal computers jumped 16 percent in the first quarter vs. a year earlier, according to research firm International Data Corp.
It said U.S. shipments rose 20 percent, the fastest of any major region, and the best quarterly domestic growth rate since the end of 1995.

Among high-tech stocks, Cisco Systems Inc., the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, was up 3/8 at 46-3/4. Intel Corp. was up 2-3/8 at 146-1/4. Dell Computer Corp. rose 2-1/4 at 80. Sun Microsystems Inc. gained 1-1/8 at 28-1/4.
